summary.text: A 25-year-old primigravida at 20 weeks of gestation, initially diagnosed with a single live intrauterine pregnancy, was referred in July 2024 with severe epigastric pain, burning micturition, intermittent high-grade fever, palpitations and multiple episodes of vomiting for the past 2-3 days. The patient was admitted to the ICU with hypovolemic shock, blood pressure 90/50 mmHg, SpO2 94% on room air, pallor and abdominal guarding, tenderness and rigidity.

External ultrasound showed a single live intrauterine fetus corresponding to 19.4 weeks with a normal anomaly scan; ultrasonography demonstrated moderate hemoperitoneum, heterogeneous hepatic echo-texture and splenic parenchymal abnormalities, and paracentesis yielded hemorrhagic fluid. Admission hemoglobin was 7 g/dL with leukocytosis and platelets of 220×10^3/mm^3 described as thrombocytopenia. The provisional diagnosis was acute gastroenteritis with hypovolemic shock and sepsis.

Over 5-6 hours the abdominal signs worsened and hemoglobin dropped from 8 to 5.6 g/dL; one unit of packed cell volume was transfused immediately, and an urgent exploratory laparotomy was performed; one unit of PCV and two units of fresh frozen plasma were transfused. About one liter of hemoperitoneum was evacuated and an intact 20×25 cm left ampullary tubal mass was exteriorized, diagnosed as an unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy, and removed.

Sectioning the mass showed a fetus of about 20 weeks weighing 419 g with placenta; the fetus, initially assessed as viable on operative ultrasonography, was non-viable after removal, and histopathology confirmed tubal ectopic pregnancy. Postoperatively the patient remained hemodynamically stable and was discharged on the fifth day; the authors relate the missed diagnosis to ultrasonography only in the second trimester in a patient of lower socioeconomic background.

article_limitations: No sex/gender noun or pronoun refers to the patient, so documented_sex is not recorded; primigravida is not treated as a sex statement.
Discussion paragraphs b00010 to b00012 describe published cases cited from the literature and are not index-patient facts; b00001, b00004, b00008, b00009 and b00014 are general background.
The platelet count of 220×10^(3)/mm^(3) is called thrombocytopenia by the source; both are kept literally and the discrepancy is not resolved.
The admission hemoglobin of 7 g/dL and the cited starting value of 8 g/dL for the later drop are kept as separate observations without reconciliation.
Whether the trailing duration (the past 2-3 days) covers all listed presenting complaints is not explicit; it is applied to each with a note.
The source lists no supplements and no tables; three single-panel figures were viewed separately in visual.json.
Exteriorization and clamp/removal of the mass are not ordered relative to each other (paragraph order only); removal is ordered before sectioning by "after removal".
